1-2-1.title: Pre-independence era
1-2-1.explanation: Formal psychology education in India began in the early 20th century within a colonial education system. The uploaded NET material traces an important institutional beginning to Calcutta University: Sir Asutosh Mukherjee promoted Experimental Psychology in the postgraduate curriculum; Brojendra Nath Seal prepared the 1905 syllabus and established a laboratory. The laboratory was later upgraded into the first Department of Experimental Psychology. Research there included depth perception, psychophysics and attention. Psychology was included as a separate section of the Indian Science Congress in 1923; the Indian Psychological Association was founded in 1924 and the Indian Journal of Psychology appeared in 1925. 1-2-2.title: Post-independence era
1-2-2.explanation: The source describes post-independence psychology as expanding institutionally while remaining strongly influenced by its philosophical and Western scientific inheritance. After 1947, psychology was linked with nation-building and research. Departments expanded in universities such as Mysore and Patna; the University Grants Commission, established in 1956, supported university development. Applied and clinical psychology also expanded through institutions including NCERT and mental-health centres. The source notes that many psychology departments had emerged from philosophy departments, creating a continuing tension between philosophical roots and the aspiration to establish psychology as an experimental science. 1-2-3.title: 1970s social issues
1-2-3.explanation: During the 1970s, the source describes a shift toward socially relevant psychological research. Concerns included communal violence, social conflict and problems that were difficult to understand through culturally neutral laboratory approaches alone. The UNESCO-supported work associated with Gardner Murphy investigated communal violence and culminated in the 1953 volume In the Minds of Men; the later historical account presents this tradition as part of psychology's growing engagement with Indian social problems. The period also contributed to criticism that psychology should address the realities of Indian society rather than simply reproduce Western research. 1-5-2.title: Functionalism
1-5-2.explanation: Functionalism shifted attention from analysing the contents of consciousness to the functions of mental activity and behaviour. William James is the central association. The approach asks how mind and behaviour help people function, adapt and respond to their surroundings.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Functionalism asks about function, not just elements.

1-5-2.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from ciccarelli-white, self-teaching-guide, powerwithin.
1-5-2.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Functionalism shifted attention from analysing the contents of consciousness to the functions of mental activity and behaviour. William James is the central association. The approach asks how mind and behaviour help people function, adapt and respond to their surroundings.

KEY POINTS

• functions of mind
• everyday functioning

1-5-3.title: Psychoanalytical psychology
1-5-3.explanation: Psychoanalytical psychology, as presented in the supplied sources, centres on unconscious processes, conflict and the influence of repressed wishes and experiences on behaviour. Freud's model includes id, ego and superego; psychoanalysis aims to bring repressed unconscious material into consciousness and develop insight.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Do not reduce psychoanalysis to one motive.

1-5-3.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from baron-misra, self-teaching-guide, powerwithin.
1-5-3.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Psychoanalytical psychology, as presented in the supplied sources, centres on unconscious processes, conflict and the influence of repressed wishes and experiences on behaviour. Freud's model includes id, ego and superego; psychoanalysis aims to bring repressed unconscious material into consciousness and develop insight.

KEY POINTS
• Freud
• unconscious processes
• repression
• id, ego, superego
• pleasure principle
• insight

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
Do not confuse repression with rationalization. Repression removes threatening material from conscious awareness, whereas rationalization supplies a rational-sounding explanation for a failure or transgression.

HOW TO APPLY
If a stem describes symptoms as indirect expressions of repressed wishes or asks about bringing unconscious material into consciousness, retrieve the psychoanalytic framework.

MEMORY HOOK
Psychoanalysis → unconscious conflict → repression → insight

1-5-4.title: Gestalt psychology
1-5-4.explanation: Gestalt psychology argues that psychological experience, especially perception, cannot always be understood by simply adding isolated sensory elements. The organised pattern or whole matters. Wertheimer, Koffka and Köhler are central figures.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Gestalt is broader than insight learning.

1-5-4.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from ciccarelli-white, self-teaching-guide, powerwithin.
1-5-4.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Gestalt psychology argues that psychological experience, especially perception, cannot always be understood by simply adding isolated sensory elements. The organised pattern or whole matters. Wertheimer, Koffka and Köhler are central figures.

KEY POINTS
• organized whole
• pattern/configuration
• Wertheimer
• perception
• insight learning

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
The key contrast is whole versus isolated elements. Structuralism analyses elements; Gestalt psychology emphasizes the organisation and pattern in which those elements are experienced.

HOW TO APPLY
When a question describes a melody, visual pattern or apparent movement whose experience depends on the relationship among parts, identify the Gestalt principle rather than an element-by-element analysis.

MEMORY HOOK
Gestalt → organized whole → pattern

1-5-5.title: Behaviorism
1-5-5.explanation: Behaviorism redirected psychology toward observable behaviour and away from treating private consciousness as the primary scientific object. John B. Watson is the central founding figure in the classical school; later behaviourism developed conditioning and reinforcement traditions.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Negative reinforcement increases behavior.

1-5-5.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from self-teaching-guide, ciccarelli-white, powerwithin.
1-5-5.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Behaviorism redirected psychology toward observable behaviour and away from treating private consciousness as the primary scientific object. John B. Watson is the central founding figure in the classical school; later behaviourism developed conditioning and reinforcement traditions.

KEY POINTS
• John B. Watson
• observable behaviour
• stimulus-response
• conditioning

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
Behaviorism is not structuralism's analysis of conscious experience. Watson argued that psychology should study behaviour itself rather than an unobservable mind or consciousness.

1-5-6.title: Humanistic-Existential psychology
1-5-6.explanation: The supplied NET framework treats Humanistic-Existential psychology as a major reaction against narrow accounts of people. Its emphasis is on subjective experience, meaning, agency, personal growth and the individual's relationship with existence rather than reducing behaviour to only observable responses or unconscious drives.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Humanistic psychology is not merely positive thinking.

1-5-7.title: Transpersonal psychology
1-5-7.explanation: The supplied NET framework places Transpersonal psychology among approaches that extend psychological inquiry beyond ordinary personal identity and include altered or expanded states of consciousness and spiritual dimensions of experience. In the supplied Indian-psychology material, consciousness and self-knowledge are also central themes, making the distinction between transpersonal and mainstream personal-level accounts especially important.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: It is not identical to any single religion.

4-2-1.title: Neuron structure
4-2-1.explanation: A neuron is a specialised information-processing and information-transmitting cell. Its major structural regions are the soma (cell body), dendrites, axon and terminal buttons. Dendrites generally receive incoming information, the soma maintains the cell and integrates inputs, and the axon carries the neural message toward terminal regions.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Dendrites and axons have different typical roles.

4-2-1.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from powerwithin, ciccarelli-white, baron-misra.
4-2-1.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
A neuron is a specialised information-processing and information-transmitting cell. Its major structural regions are the soma (cell body), dendrites, axon and terminal buttons. Dendrites generally receive incoming information, the soma maintains the cell and integrates inputs, and the axon carries the neural message toward terminal regions.

KEY POINTS
• soma
• dendrites
• axon
• axon terminals
• myelin

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
Dendrites and axons have different typical directions of information flow: dendrites receive toward the cell body, whereas the axon carries the neural message away toward terminals. Myelin insulates axons and can increase conduction speed.

HOW TO APPLY
For a structure-function question, map the part to its role: dendrite = receiving, soma = cell body, axon = conducting, terminal = communicating with the next cell.

MEMORY HOOK
Dendrite in → soma integrates → axon out → terminal communicates

4-2-3.title: Types of neurons
4-2-3.explanation: Neurons can be distinguished by their role in information flow. Sensory (afferent) neurons carry information toward the central nervous system, motor (efferent) neurons carry commands away from the CNS to effectors, and interneurons connect neural pathways within the CNS.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Afferent/efferent are defined relative to the CNS.

4-2-3.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Neurons can be distinguished by their role in information flow. Sensory (afferent) neurons carry information toward the central nervous system, motor (efferent) neurons carry commands away from the CNS to effectors, and interneurons connect neural pathways within the CNS.

KEY POINTS
• sensory/afferent
• motor/efferent
• interneurons
• direction of information flow

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
Afferent means toward the CNS; efferent means away from the CNS. The distinction is about direction of information flow, not whether a neuron is physically located in the brain or spinal cord.

HOW TO APPLY
If a PYQ asks whether a pathway carries sensory information toward the CNS or motor commands away from it, use the afferent/efferent direction rule first.

4-2-4.title: Neural impulse
4-2-4.explanation: Neural signalling within an axon depends on changes in membrane potential. At rest the neuron maintains a resting potential; sufficient stimulation reaches threshold and initiates an action potential. Depolarization is followed by repolarization and a refractory phase.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Stimulus intensity is not coded by larger action potentials.

4-2-4.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from powerwithin, baron-misra, ciccarelli-white.
4-2-4.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Neural signalling within an axon depends on changes in membrane potential. At rest the neuron maintains a resting potential; sufficient stimulation reaches threshold and initiates an action potential. Depolarization is followed by repolarization and a refractory phase.

KEY POINTS
• resting potential
• threshold
• depolarization
• repolarization
• refractory phase
• all-or-none

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
An action potential is not graded in amplitude: once threshold is reached, the action potential follows an all-or-none pattern. In myelinated axons, saltatory conduction makes the signal appear to jump between nodes of Ranvier.

HOW TO APPLY
When a question asks what happens after threshold, retrieve the sequence: depolarization → repolarization → refractory period.

MEMORY HOOK
Threshold → depolarize → repolarize → refractory

CORE CONCEPT
Related issues in classical conditioning include processes such as acquisition, extinction, stimulus generalization and discrimination, and spontaneous recovery. These phenomena concern how conditioned responses are established, weakened, generalized or recovered over time.

KEY POINTS
• Acquisition is the development of a conditioned response.
• Extinction follows when the conditioned stimulus is no longer paired with the unconditioned stimulus.
• Generalization extends responding to similar stimuli.
• Discrimination involves learning to respond differently to distinct stimuli; spontaneous recovery is the return of an extinguished response after a delay.
